summary: Iteration 6 backend + frontend tested for combined LRM+AMZ mapping, sku_mappings collection, canonical marketplaces list, idempotency, and dashboards. 14/14 new iteration6 tests PASS. 18/19 regression tests (iter3+iter4) PASS — the single failure is a stale hardcoded ASIN assumption in legacy test_iteration4 (SAND_116_15x20_white was mapped to B00PB8WM4S in iter4 seed but the new canonical lrm_amz_map.xlsx maps it to B01M18XNNS; invariant is intact, the test data assumption is outdated). Frontend Marketplaces page shows all 16 canonical filter pills including Ambiance Web/Appros/Zooplus placeholders. Frontend Products page top rows show merchant SKUs (col-, SAND_/SAND-, J-, J3-, roll-) with realistic COGS and margin %. Critical invariants verified: (a) Amazon line_key always ends with ASIN (^PO::B[0-9A-Z]{9}$), (b) re-upload of amazon_po.xls inserts=0 and Amazon Vendor total stays at 6,580, (c) re-upload of beezup.xlsx inserts=0 and Leroy Merlin total stays stable, (d) sku field holds merchant_sku while asin field preserves the ASIN.

minor.issue: Returned margin_pct=63.41% and revenue €398,832 / cogs €113,658 — the review request mentioned 'expected revenue ~119k, margin ~66%, cogs ~27k'. The actual numbers reflect all channels (not just Amazon). If the expected figure was Amazon-only, no bug; otherwise the figure spec may be stale. Numbers ARE substantially different from pre-mapping (cogs > 1000, margin_pct in 30-95 range), so the qualitative expectation holds.
(Carry-over from iter 4) Still no admin-role check — any authenticated user can rewrite the entire sku_mappings collection.
(Carry-over from iter 4/5) No 'source' query filter — must use marketplaces='Amazon Vendor' to count Amazon PO orders.
(Carry-over from iter 5) No DELETE/PATCH endpoint exposed for individual sku_mappings entries.

issues: Channel performance chart top section shows only non-Amazon channels (Amazon Vendor pill exists but Amazon Vendor bar absent from the chart — verify whether this is intentional date-range filter or if the chart should include Amazon Vendor by default).

action_items: (Cosmetic) Update legacy /app/backend/tests/test_iteration4.py::test_orders_query_returns_mapped_sku_with_asin_preserved — its hardcoded ASIN B00PB8WM4S → SAND_116_15x20_white pair no longer matches canonical lrm_amz_map (which uses B01M18XNNS for the same merchant SKU). Replace with a dynamic lookup or drop the assertion.
Add admin-role check to POST /api/uploads/asin-mapping (and POST /api/uploads/orders, /api/uploads/costs, PUT /api/cost-constants) — these are admin-only operations.
(Carry-over) Split server.py (1,623 lines) into routers/uploads.py, routers/asin.py, routers/marketplaces.py, parsers/*.py.

(Optional) Verify whether the Marketplaces page chart should include Amazon Vendor by default — Amazon Vendor pill is in the filter row but no Amazon Vendor bar shows on the channel-performance chart.

_remap_amazon_orders (server.py:877-918) iterates Amazon orders by asin field and Leroy Merlin orders by line_key suffix — correct strategy, uses bulk_write batches of 500.

CANONICAL_MARKETPLACES (server.py:1429-1446) is exactly 16 entries; list_marketplaces merges DB distinct values with canonical list so empty placeholders (Ambiance Web, Appros, Zooplus) always render — verified live.
Mirror to legacy asin_mappings only for Amazon Vendor rows (server.py:821-827) — good backward compat; Leroy Merlin entries live only in sku_mappings.

context_for_next_testing_agent: DB state at end of iter6: 6,580 Amazon orders, ~1,300 BeezUP/ChannelEngine orders, sku_mappings has ~47,418 entries (Amazon Vendor + Leroy Merlin + TEST_BACK_COMPAT_ASIN). Idempotency invariant holds: line_key suffix is always ASIN for Amazon; sku field is merchant_sku; re-upload of amazon_po.xls or beezup.xlsx returns inserted=0. To re-run: pytest /app/backend/tests/test_iteration6.py -v (14 tests, ~38s). The legacy iter4 test_orders_query_returns_mapped_sku_with_asin_preserved fails on a stale hardcoded ASIN — not a regression.
rca of the issue: No production bug. The only failing regression test (test_iteration4) has a stale data assumption — it asserted SAND_116_15x20_white maps from B00PB8WM4S, but the canonical lrm_amz_map.xlsx now maps it from B01M18XNNS. The invariant (asin field preserved, sku=merchant_sku, line_key=PO::ASIN) is fully satisfied on the returned record. Fix: update the test to either pick a non-conflicting ASIN/SKU pair or assert structural invariants only.
